how_to_score: Give a fresh agent only SKILL.md, the context, and one request at a time. The agent passes a case when it picks the expected command, shows the menu for expect menu without running anything, asks exactly one question naming every listed option for expect ask, or for expect error and expect no-match runs nothing, says why, and lists every area in the context.

cases.why: No argument, so the menu shows and nothing runs.

cases.request: Go through the review comments on our merged PRs and tell me which conventions reviewers keep asking for.
We have no coding standards. Build some for this repo from its review history.
cases.why: Standards from nothing start at mine, because write needs clusters.json.

cases.request: clusters.json is done. Turn the top conventions into standards in the repo.
Generate the standards as one skill per area instead of a single index.
cases.why: Output shape B is a write option.

cases.request: Check my branch against our coding standards before I open the pull request.
Does PR 482 break any of our § rules?
Which of our standards would agents follow anyway without being told? Cut those out.
A/B test whether the rule about mapping documents to DTOs still changes what agents write.
Half the files our standards cite got moved in the refactor. Which rules are pointing at nothing?

cases.why: Cleaning up could mean deleting rules agents already follow, or finding rules that drifted from the code.

cases.request: Are our standards still any good?
cases.why: Still good could mean still matching the code, or still needed by agents.
A scope with no command means review of that scope, which only reads.
A § with no command is a scope, so it routes to review of that area's lenses.
Review accepts a §, which applies only that lens.
Prune accepts an area and tests only its rules.
Write accepts an area and refreshes only it.
Mine takes only a path or glob, because areas don't exist before write. The reply says so and lists the areas.
billing/ is no §, no area slug and no tracked path, so the reply says it matched nothing, lists the areas and stops.

context: Generated standards exist. Their index has three areas: §1 data-access (rules §1.1 to §1.3), §2 error-handling (rules §2.1 to §2.4) and §3 testing (rules §3.1 and §3.2). The repo tracks files under src/api/ and src/jobs/, and nothing under billing/.
